name: Moped
description: The lowest-powered motor driven cycle: a motor of 2 brake horsepower (1,500 W) or less that can reach between 20 and 30 mph within a mile, with or without pedals. An electric motor qualifies on power alone; the 50 cc limit applies only to combustion engines.

restrictions.rule: A motor driven cycle, with or without pedals, whose motor produces 2 brake horsepower (1,500 W) or less
The speed it can reach within one mile is at least 20 mph and no more than 30 mph
A combustion engine may not exceed 50 cc or make the rider shift gears; failing any of these criteria makes it a motor driven cycle that needs a Class L license
restrictions.citation: Illinois Vehicle Code §1-148.2; 92 Ill. Adm. Code 1030.30

restrictions.rule: Riders need a valid driver's license of any classification; no motorcycle classification is needed
Rider and passenger must wear glasses, goggles or a face shield unless it has a windshield that rises above the rider's eyes
Titled and registered with the Secretary of State, carries a license plate, and must carry liability insurance
Carries a passenger only if built for two, with a passenger seat and footrests
The Department of Transportation may bar motor driven cycles, mopeds included, from controlled access highways it signs
As a motor driven cycle it may not be ridden on sidewalks, bike lanes, bicycle paths, shared-use paths, bike trails or interstate highways
restrictions.citation: Illinois Vehicle Code §11-1403.4, added by SB 3484 (2026)
